Welcome to Potley Hill Primary School
Each and every child is welcomed and valued as an individual, and we aspire to provide a happy and caring environment where every child, regardless of their background, can flourish as a unique individual whilst also contributing to our school community.
Our curriculum is both challenging and creative, catering for the diverse needs of our children. Through our curriculum at Potley Hill, we aim to inspire an excitement and enthusiasm for learning while catering for the diverse needs of our children. The curriculum aims to equip pupils with key, lifelong skills across a wide range of subjects but it is underpinned by high quality English and Maths. We also encourage the development of a broad range of interests and talents by providing a rich variety of extra-curricular activities, opportunities and experiences which are supported through our Potley Hill Pupil Guarantee.

pageCache.pageTitle: Potley Hill Primary School  - Sports Premium
pageCache.text:
Sports Premium
At Potley Hill, we are passionate about sports. Our vision is for all children to be engaged in high quality physical activity, whilst ensuring that they know and understand the benefits of keeping healthy. We strive to ignite enthusiasm in all our children to be regularly active, physically confident and to develop a passion for exercise outside of the school day. Through physical activity, we aim to improve health and well-being, to promote active participation and develop high self-esteem and high expectations within every child. As a school, we endeavour to inspire all pupils to succeed and excel in competitive sports and other physically demanding activities, embedding values such as: communication, team work, respect, resilience, ambition and attitude.
The government provides additional funding to improve provision of physical education (PE) and sport in schools. This funding is provided jointly by the Departments for Education, Health and Culture, Media and Sport. The funding is ring-fenced and therefore can only be spent on provision of PE and sport in schools.
In Key Stage 2, children have swimming lessons at St Neots Preparatory School swimming pool. These lessons are taught by qualified swimming teachers and please see our most recent swimming results below.

Prospective Parents (Admissions)
We look forward to meeting you and working with you to provide your child with the best start to their education!
Prospective Parents Tours
Is your child due to start school in September 2027? If so, why not come and see the school for yourself on one of our 'Prospective Parent Tours?' The tours are scheduled to take place on the following dates:
Wednesday 7th October 2026 at 09:30am
Thursday 15th October 2026 at 9.30am
Wednesday 25th November 2026 at 9.30am
Thursday 7th January 2027at 9.30am
To book a place on one of these tours please do not hesitate to contact the School Office on 01252 876106, or email adminoffice@potleyhill.hants.sch.uk.
All ‘in-year applications' are managed by Hampshire County Council Admissions Team and further information about the application process can be found at the following link 'Applying for a school place in-year'. Alternatively, contact Hampshire general enquiries on 0300 555 1377. The Hampshire County Council Website will give you guidance on how to choose the right school for your child: https://www.hants.gov.uk/educationandlearning/admissions
For anyone wishing to complete an ‘in-year transfer’ between schools, we warmly invite parents, along with their children, to see the school for yourselves, so please do not hesitate to contact the School Office on 01252 876106, or by emailing adminoffice@potleyhill.hants.sch.uk to arrange an appointment. Alternatively, there is a wide range of information available on this website which provides a comprehensive picture of the school, but please do not hesitate to contact us should you require any further information.
Once you have completed an application for an ‘in-year transfer’, we will write to you with the outcome and if we are unable to offer a place, your child’s name will be added to our waiting list.

pageCache.pageTitle: Potley Hill Primary School  - Pupil Premium
pageCache.text:
Pupil Premium
The designated person responsible for the leadership of Pupil Premium across the school is: Mrs. Elaine Morris (Acting Assistant Headteacher and SENCo).
Pupil premium is additional funding for schools from the government. Pupil premium is provided to help raise the attainment and achievement of disadvantaged children.
At Potley Hill Primary School, we believe that if you get it right for disadvantaged children, you get it right for everybody. Our inclusive culture, with high expectations for all, ensures we maximise opportunities for every child so as to develop confident and successful learners. Potley Hill’s mindset is to ensure there is an expectation of accelerated progress for all. The culture of our school fosters strong relationships with all stakeholders of it so that we know our children and parents well.
We focus on ensuring all children have enriching and challenging access to a broad and balanced curriculum. We pride ourselves on providing all children with a range of life skills, as well as resilience and a positive attitude so that they can continue to make excellent progress across the school and as they move on to the next stage of their education.
We pride ourselves in knowing all of our children well across the school, delivering a personalised curriculum which meets all their needs. Every member of staff understands the key groupings across the schools and knows how to develop specific skills for individual children.
Teachers work closely together to ensure a smooth transition between each year group, with joint planning and moderation meetings throughout the year to support each other and provide useful information and feedback about all children. As a result, every staff member has an excellent knowledge of all children and expectations are consistent across the school in order to ensure children are continually challenged and make the best possible progress.
We recognise that Early Years is incredibly important and that a successful start to Primary education is paramount. Our Early Years curriculum is exciting and stimulating, with all children having new and unique experiences.
The role of the Pupil Premium Leader is to ensure all staff are aware of the different groupings across the school and to make sure that there is a balance of funding for enrichment, pastoral care and progress across the curriculum. It is also to monitor and regularly review the impact of this extra funding.
Key Aspects of the role include:
Potley Hill Primary uses seven key building blocks to support disadvantaged pupils’ achievement:
Carrying out learning walks and lesson observations
Working alongside teachers to team teach
Delivering training to all staff
Reporting to Governors
Whole school ethos of attainment for all

pageCache.pageTitle: Potley Hill Primary School  - British Values
pageCache.text:
British Values
In November 2014, the Department for Education (DfE) produced non-statutory guidance on how schools should promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs as part of spiritual, moral, social, and cultural (SMSC) development. These core British values were first articulated in the Government’s ‘Prevent’ strategy of 2011.
At Potley Hill, we take our responsibility very seriously to prepare children positively for life in modern Britain. We ensure that the fundamental British values are introduced, discussed and lived through the ethos, values and work of the school. All curriculum areas provide a vehicle for furthering understanding of these concepts and, in particular, our RE, SMSC and PSHE lessons provide excellent opportunities to deepen and develop understanding.

Absence Request
Information for parents/carers:
At Potley Hill Primary School we believe that regular school attendance is essential if children are to achieve their full potential. We value the attendance of all pupils. Missing out on lessons leaves children vulnerable to falling behind and can put them at risk of wider harm. There is a wide range of evidence as to the health and wellbeing benefits of school-age education. Research commissioned by the Department for Education shows missing school for even a day can mean a child is less likely to achieve good grades, which can have a damaging effect on their life chances
Headteachers must continue to comply with the 2013 amendment to the Education (Pupil Registration) (England) (2006) Regulations 2013 which means that they cannot authorise a leave of absence from school unless it is exceptional.
Parents/carers must comply with Section 444 of the Education Act 1996 that states that
“(1) If a child of compulsory school age who is a registered pupil at a school fails to attend regularly at the school, his parent is guilty of an offence.”
“(1A) If in the circumstances mentioned in subsection (1) the parent knows that his child is failing to attend regularly at the school and fails without reasonable justification to cause him to do so, he is guilty of an offence.”
Parents and carers can fail to comply with section 444 of the Education Act if their child has unauthorised absences, even if those unauthorised absences are for a family holiday.
All Local Authorities and their Headteachers must continue to follow the law on attendance and implement the government’s guidance around attendance. This remains the legal expectation for all education authorities, and supports children in attending their statutory entitlement of 190 days per year.
It is of vital importance that all of us – the local authority, families, schools and children – do all we can to ensure children achieve the highest levels of attendance.

SEND
Our SENCo is Mrs Elaine Morris.
At Potley Hill Primary School, we strive to support all children to enable them to achieve at school. In order to do this, many steps are taken to support them through their learning journey. High Quality Teaching is vital; however for some children there are occasions when further additional support may be needed to help them to maximise their potential for learning. At this point, children might be identified as having a Special Educational Need (SEN). This will mean that the child receives extra support so that they can make progress in their learning.
We endeavour to provide an inclusive education for all children, the majority of this comes from within the school but sometimes we refer to outside agencies.
Hampshire’s Local Offer, (co-produced with parents, carers and young people), aims to help you find your way through the maze of information to reach the best solutions for you / your child and includes information about education, health, social care, preparation for adulthood, leisure services and impartial information advice and support.
To see Hampshire's Local Offer click here or contact our SENCO Mrs Morris via the email address: senco@potleyhill.hants.sch.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: Potley Hill Primary School  - Performance Data and OFSTED Information
pageCache.text:
Performance Data and OFSTED Information
The publication of Key Stage 2 data for the academic year 2025-26 showed the performance of pupils at Potley Hill Primary School was above the national average in all areas used by the government to measure school performance. This was also the case with the majority of other performance indicators across the school including the Year 4 Multiplication Check, the Year 1 Phonics Screening together with Early Years outcomes.
The attainment levels of pupils at the end of Key Stage 2 in Grammar, Punctuation and Spelling (GPS) far exceeded national outcomes for the second consecutive year with 95% of pupils achieving the expected standard with 60% of pupils achieving the greater depth standard. These results were 22% and 28% higher than the national average, which is an incredibly positive achievement. Reading is also a significant strength with 88% of Year 6 pupils working at the expected standard and 43% working at the greater depth standard, which is also 13% and 14% above the national average. This significant strength in reading is also demonstrated in Year 1 as 97% of pupils achieved the threshold in the Year 1 Phonics Screening, which is 17% higher than last year's national average (24-25 National Average will be released in October 2025).
The information above describes the 'good' academic outcomes achieved by pupils compared to the national average, which is also detailed in the OFSTED Report of October 2024, (which can be found below). The many strengths of the school were celebrated within the report, with all areas judged as being 'good' by OFSTED, with the exception being the behaviour and attitudes of pupils which received a judgement of 'outstanding.'
